## ① Asymptotic notation
| | means | definition |
|---|---|---|
| $O$ | $\le$ | $\exists c,n_0: 0\le f\le c\,g\ \forall n\ge n_0$ |
| $\Omega$ | $\ge$ | $\exists c,n_0: 0\le c\,g\le f$ |
| $\Theta$ | $=$ | $O$ **and** $\Omega$ |
| $o$ | $<$ | $\lim f/g=0$ |
| $\omega$ | $>$ | $\lim f/g=\infty$ |

**Limit test** $L=\lim f/g$: $0<L<\infty\Rightarrow\Theta$; $L=0\Rightarrow o$; $L=\infty\Rightarrow\omega$.

$1<\log n<\sqrt n<n<n\log n<n^2<n^3<2^n<n!<n^n$
- poly: leading term only, $\sum c_in^i=O(n^d)$
- $\log_b n=\Theta(\log n)$ — base irrelevant **in Θ**, not in exponent
- $(\log n)^a=o(n^b)$; $n^d=o(r^n)$, $r>1$; $r^n=o(s^n)$, $r<s$
- **Compare by rewriting as $2^{(\cdot)}$:** $2^{\log n}=n$, $n^{\log n}=2^{\log^2 n}$, $a^{\log n}=n^{\log a}$
> [!warn] $f=O(g)\not\Rightarrow 2^f=O(2^g)$ ($4n$ vs $2n$: $4^n\to\infty$). But $f^2=O(g^2)$ ✓, $\log f=O(\log g)$ ✓ ($g\ge2$).

**Prove Θ of loops:** upper = loop bounds; lower = count an expensive chunk ($i\le n/4,\ j\ge 3n/4$ ⇒ $\ge n^3/32$).
**Efficient** = polynomial in input size. Worst case default.

#### Sums & logs
$\sum i=\frac{n(n+1)}2$ · $\sum i^2=\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}6$ · $\sum i^3=(\sum i)^2$
$\sum_{0}^{n} r^i=\frac{r^{n+1}-1}{r-1}$, $\sum_0^n 2^i=2^{n+1}-1$
$\log ab=\log a+\log b$, $\log a^k=k\log a$, $a^{\log_b n}=n^{\log_b a}$

## ⊕ Recurrences
**Unroll:** $2T(\frac n2)+cn=2^kT(\frac n{2^k})+kcn$, stop $k=\lg n$ ⇒ $cn\lg n+cn$.
**Tree:** cost/level × #levels; depth $\log_b n$, leaves $a^{\log_b n}=n^{\log_b a}$. Geometric: biggest term dominates (root ↓, leaves ↑).
**Guess+induct:** same constant both sides; never "$\le O(\cdot)$" inside IH.
> [!info] **Master** $T=aT(n/b)+f$, compare $f$ vs $n^{\log_b a}$:
> ① $f=O(n^{\log_b a-\epsilon})$ ⇒ $\Theta(n^{\log_b a})$ (leaves)
> ② $f=\Theta(n^{\log_b a})$ ⇒ $\Theta(n^{\log_b a}\log n)$
> ③ $f=\Omega(n^{\log_b a+\epsilon})$ & $af(n/b)\le cf(n)$, $c<1$ ⇒ $\Theta(f)$

$aT(\frac nb)+n^d$: $d>\log_ba\to n^d$; $=\to n^d\log n$; $<\to n^{\log_ba}$

| recurrence | solution | e.g. |
|---|---|---|
| $T(\frac n2)+1$ | $\log n$ | binary search |
| $T(\frac n2)+n$ | $n$ | |
| $2T(\frac n2)+1$ | $n$ | tree traversal |
| $2T(\frac n2)+n$ | $n\log n$ | mergesort, closest pair |
| $3T(\frac n2)+n$ | $n^{\lg3}\approx n^{1.59}$ | Karatsuba |
| $4T(\frac n2)+n$ | $n^2$ | naive mult |
| $T(\frac n5)+T(\frac{7n}{10})+n$ | $n$ | median of medians |
| $2T(\frac n2)+n\log n$ | $n\log^2n$ | (no Master) |
| $T(n-1)+n$ | $n^2$ | quickselect worst |
| $T(n-1)+1$ | $n$ | |

**Akra–Bazzi:** $\sum a_iT(n/b_i)+f$: find $\rho$ with $\sum a_i b_i^{-\rho}=1$; $T=\Theta(n^\rho(1+\int_1^n \frac{f(u)}{u^{\rho+1}}du))$.
> [!warn] Master fails on: unequal splits, $T(n-1)$, non-polynomial gaps ($n\log n$ vs $n$), case ③ w/o regularity. $\lg 3=\log_2 3$, not $\log_3 2$.

## ✎ Proof templates
**Induction:** ① state $P(n)$ ② base ③ IH: $P(k)$ for **some** $k$ ④ step: prove $P(k{+}1)$, *mark where IH used* ⑤ conclude ∀$n\ge$ base. Strong induction: assume all $\le k$.
**Structural (graphs/trees):** take **arbitrary** $(k{+}1)$-object, *remove* leaf/vertex/source → IH → add back. Never grow a $k$-object.
**Loop invariant:** init (holds before 1st iter) · maintenance $I(i)\Rightarrow I(i+1)$ · exit+inv ⇒ goal · termination (bounded monotone var). Sorting inv must say "**permutation of original**".
**Algorithm correctness:** soundness (output right, strong induction on size) + completeness (terminates; each call shrinks).
**Contradiction · contrapositive ($\neg Q\Rightarrow\neg P$) · cases · counterexample** (one suffices; test past small cases: $2^{11}-1=23\cdot89$).
> [!bad] A "proof" that restates the algorithm, or only a picture, gets no credit.

## ▷ Stable matching (Gale–Shapley)
Perfect + **no instability** ($m$ prefers $w'$, $w'$ prefers $m$). Free $m$ proposes to best untried $w$; $w$ trades up only. ≤ $n^2$ proposals → $O(n^2)$ with `Next[m]`, `Current[w]`, `Ranking[w][m]` (O(1) compare). Output man-optimal. Brute force $n!$; input size $\Theta(n^2)$.

## ⊕ Graphs basics
$n=|V|$, $m=|E|\le\binom n2$. **Handshake** $\sum\deg=2m$ (core of every $O(n+m)$ proof).
**Tree:** connected + acyclic ⇔ connected with $m=n-1$ ⇔ unique $u$–$v$ path. $\ge2$ leaves if $n\ge2$ (endpoints of longest path). Binary tree: #2-child nodes $=L-1$.

| rep | space | edge? | neighbours |
|---|---|---|---|
| adj. list | $O(n+m)$ | $O(\deg)$ | $O(\deg)$ |
| adj. matrix | $O(n^2)$ | $O(1)$ | $O(n)$ |

**BFS** (queue): layers $L_i$ = dist $i$ → unweighted shortest paths; non-tree edges span ≤1 layer. Mark visited on **enqueue**.
**DFS** (stack/recursion): non-tree edges ancestor–descendant (undirected). Directed: back edge ⇔ cycle.
**Components:** outer loop `for s: if unseen: BFS/DFS(s)` — still $O(n+m)$ total.
**Bipartite** ⇔ no odd cycle: 2-colour BFS layers; same-layer edge ⇒ odd cycle. $O(n+m)$.
> [!warn] Iterative DFS pops neighbours in **reverse** — push reversed to match recursive order.

## ⊕ Directed: SCC · DAG · topo
**Strongly connected?** search from $s$ in $G$ **and** $G^{rev}$ both reach all. $O(n+m)$.
**Kosaraju:** ① DFS on $G$, push on **finish** ② reverse graph ③ pop; DFS in $G^{rev}$ = one SCC. $O(n+m)$. SCC-condensation is a DAG.
**DAG ⇔ topological order.** Every DAG has a source (walk back $n{+}1$ steps → repeat → cycle). Induct: remove source, order rest.
**Kahn:** queue indeg-0; pop, output, decrement; <$n$ output ⇒ cycle. $O(n+m)$. Or DFS reverse finish order. Orders not unique.

#### Worked patterns
**Trace** edges 1–2,1–9,2–6,2–5,2–3,3–7,4–6,8–9 from 1: BFS `1 2 9 6 5 3 8 4 7`; DFS `1 2 6 4 5 3 7 9 8`. State neighbour order.
**Pigeonhole:** all deg $\ge n/2$ ⇒ connected (non-adjacent $u,v$ share neighbour). Tight: $2\times K_{n/2}$.
**BFS cut node:** dist$(s,t)>n/2$ ⇒ some layer has 1 node; delete ⇒ disconnect.

## ① Greedy proof templates
**Greedy** = process in an order, best choice now, never undo. Show a rule fails: 2–4 item counterexample with greedy vs OPT values.
> **Stays ahead** (sequence + measure). ① greedy $g_1..g_k$, OPT $o_1..o_m$, same order ② claim ∀$r\le\min$: measure$(g_r)$ ≤/≥ measure$(o_r)$ ③ induct: $o_r$ still available to greedy at step $r$ ⇒ greedy's pick at least as good ④ $m>k$ ⇒ $o_{k+1}$ available after $g_k$ ⇒ greedy wouldn't stop. ⊥

> **Exchange** (shape: sorted/no gaps). ① greedy has property P (no idle, no inversions) ② OPT lacks ⇒ local defect (**adjacent** inversion / first difference) ③ swap ⇒ cost doesn't rise, others unchanged ④ strictly closer (≤ $\binom n2$ swaps) ⇒ OPT ≡ greedy. Ties = equal cost.

**First-difference form:** OPT agreeing with greedy longest; differ at $i$ ⇒ build OPT agreeing on $i$ too. ⊥
Stays ahead: intervals, Dijkstra, towers, trucks. Exchange: EDF, paging, MST, Huffman, deliveries.

## ▷ Interval scheduling
**Earliest finish first.** Sort by $f$, take if $s\ge$ last end (touching OK, `>=`). $O(n\log n)$. Stays ahead: $f(g_r)\le f(o_r)$.
❌ earliest start (long first blocks many) · ❌ shortest (short one blocks two) · ❌ fewest conflicts.
❌ **weighted**: [0,1]=$1$ vs [0,10]=$100$ → needs DP.
**Partitioning:** #resources = depth (max overlap); sort by start, heap of end times.

## ▷ Min max lateness
$l_i=\max(0,f_i-d_i)$, minimize **max**. **EDF**: sort by $d_i$, no idle. $O(n\log n)$.
❌ shortest $t$ first: (1,100),(10,10) ⇒ late 1 vs 0 · ❌ min slack: (1,2),(10,10) ⇒ late **9** vs 1.
Exchange: no idle; inversion ⇒ adjacent inversion; swap: later job ends at old $f$ with bigger $d$ ⇒ max not ↑; same-deadline orders equal.
**Supercomputer→PC:** sort **decreasing** $f_i$ (PC time). **Unit deliveries max pay:** feasible ⇔ $N_S(t)\le t$ ∀$t$; add by ↓ pay if feasible, output EDF.

## ⊕ Dijkstra (ℓ ≥ 0)
Grow $S$; add $v\notin S$ minimizing $d(u)+\ell_{uv}$. Proof: any other path leaves $S$ at $(x,y)$, already $\ge d'(y)\ge d'(v)$.
Heap: **$O(m\log n)$**; naive $O(mn)$. Settle on **extract** (tentative d can drop).
❌ negative edges. Time-dependent edges OK if FIFO ($t+w(e,t)$ nondecreasing): run on arrival times.
Tie-break fewest edges: keys (weight, #edges) or $w'=nw+1$.

## ⊕ Optimal caching
**Farthest-in-future** (offline optimal). $k=2$, `a b c b c a b` ⇒ 4 faults.
Exchange: $S$ agrees for $j$ steps; at $j{+}1$ S evicts $u$, FF $v$ ⇒ $S'$ evicts $v$, copies $S$ until $u$ requested (before $v$!) then resyncs, no extra faults.
Online ≠ optimal: FWF `1 2 3 1` (4 vs 3), LRU `1 2 3 1 3` (4 vs 3); both $k$-competitive.
Impl: next-use array (backward pass) + max-heap lazy deletion ⇒ $O(n\log k)$.

## ⊕ Minimum spanning tree
**Cut prop:** min edge crossing any cut $(S,V\setminus S)$ is in **every** MST. **Cycle prop:** max edge on any cycle is in **no** MST. (Cycle crosses a cut an **even** # times → replacement edge.)

| alg | rule | DS | time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kruskal | ↑ edges, skip cycles | union-find | $O(m\log n)$ |
| Prim | cheapest edge leaving $S$ | heap | $O(m\log n)$ |
| Rev-delete | ↓ edges, delete unless disconnects | — | — |

**Union-find:** union by rank, Find $O(\log n)$ (≈$\alpha(n)$ w/ path compression).
**Distinct costs ⇒ unique MST** (cheapest edge of $T\triangle T'$ ⊥). Ties: consistent tie-break.
**Add edge $(v,w,c)$:** path $P$ in $T$ (DFS, $O(n)$); if $c<\max P$ swap out max. MST ⇔ every non-tree edge ≥ all edges on its tree path.
**k-clustering** (max spacing): Kruskal, stop at $k$ components = drop $k{-}1$ biggest MST edges. $O(n^2\log n)$.

## ⊕ Huffman / prefix codes
Prefix code ⇔ leaves of binary tree; min ABL $=\sum f_x\,\text{depth}(x)$. Optimal tree **full**; lower freq ⇒ deeper; two rarest are **siblings at max depth**.
**Merge two lowest** freqs repeatedly; heap ⇒ $O(k\log k)$. ABL$(T)=$ABL$(T')+f_w$.
❌ top-down Shannon–Fano: .32,.25,.2,.18,.05 ⇒ 2.25 vs Huffman **2.23**.

#### Other greedy HW
**Cell towers:** leftmost uncovered house $x$ → tower at $x+4$; stays ahead $g_i\ge o_i$. **Trucks** (fixed order, fill until next doesn't fit): $g_t\ge o_t$. **Bin packing FFI** not optimal: ½−ε,½−ε,½+ε,½+ε ⇒ 3 vs 2.

## ▷ Divide & conquer
Divide → conquer (recurse) → combine. Prove: strong induction on size + combine-step correctness + each call shrinks.
**Mergesort** $2T(n/2)+n$; merge $O(n)$.
**Inversions** (pairs $i<j$, $a_i>a_j$): merge-count — when taking from **right** half, add **#remaining** in left. Return sorted list too. Ties: take left first. $O(n\log n)$.
**QuickSelect** $k$-th: partition, recurse left with $k$ or right with **$k-r$**; worst $T(n-1)+n=O(n^2)$.
**Median of medians:** groups of **5**, pivot = MoM of medians ⇒ ≥ $3n/10$ each side ⇒ $T(n/5)+T(7n/10)+n=O(n)$ (two recursive calls; groups of 3 ⇒ $n\log n$).

#### Closest pair
Pre-sort $P_x,P_y$ **once**; split by line $L$; $\delta=\min(\delta_Q,\delta_R)$. Strip: points within $\delta$ of $L$ (**each side**), sorted by $y$; compare each to next **15** ($\delta/2$ boxes, ≤1 point each; 16 apart ⇒ 3 rows ⇒ $\ge 3\delta/2$). $2T(n/2)+O(n)=O(n\log n)$; re-sorting per call ⇒ $n\log^2 n$.
**Max subarray:** max(left, right, crossing = best suffix of left + best prefix of right) ⇒ $O(n\log n)$.

## ⚠ Exam traps
> [!stop] Prove **both** directions for Θ · mark IH use · arbitrary $(k{+}1)$ instance · loop inv needs "permutation"
- Stays ahead: lemma for **every** $r$ + separate "$m>k$" step
- EDF: swap **adjacent** inversions; remove idle first; $|S|=|S^*|$ ≠ equal cost
- Lateness is $\max(0,\cdot)$; objective is **max**, not sum
- Cut ↔ **min** edge, cycle ↔ **max** edge; uniqueness needs distinct weights; bridges on no cycle
- Kosaraju stack = **finish** order, 2nd pass on $G^{rev}$
- Strongly connected needs $G$ **and** $G^{rev}$
- Don't forget combine cost ($O(n)$ merge, $O(n)$ add)
- QuickSelect right ⇒ $k-r$; MoM ⇒ 2 recursive calls
- $O(n+m)$ needs adjacency **list**; matrix ⇒ $O(n^2)$
